reading: The Presocratic Philosophers (Kirk, Raven and Schofield)
pitagoras.bio: Born on the island of Samos, Pythagoras founded a community in Croton that mixed philosophy, mathematics and a religious way of life. His followers believed that numbers reveal the order of the universe and that the soul passes from one body to another. Almost nothing he wrote survives, but his influence reached Plato and modern science.
ideas: Reality has a mathematical structure and can be understood through numbers
The soul is immortal and is reborn in other bodies, including animals
Philosophy is a way of life that purifies the soul through discipline and study
pitagoras.line: A Pythagorean follows the school founded by Pythagoras, which joined mathematics, music and spirituality. He is the founder and model of this tradition of seeking harmony.

parmenides.q: What is, is; and what is not, is not.
reading: The Presocratic Philosophers (Kirk, Raven and Schofield)
parmenides.bio: Parmenides wrote a philosophical poem in which a goddess reveals the path of truth. For him, being is one, eternal and unmoving, and the change we see is an illusion of the senses. He was the first to argue rigorously about what reality is, and almost all later Greek philosophy tried to answer him.
ideas: What is, is, and what is not, is not: nothing can come from nothing
True reality is single, eternal and unchanging
The senses deceive, and only reason can reach the truth
parmenides.line: Eleatic comes from Elea, the city where this school was born, which denied change and multiplicity. Parmenides is its founder, and his student Zeno created paradoxes to defend him.

heraclito.q: No man ever steps in the same river twice.
reading: The Presocratic Philosophers (Kirk, Raven and Schofield)
The Art and Thought of Heraclitus (Charles Kahn)
heraclito.bio: Heraclitus was an aristocrat of Ephesus famous for his enigmatic style, which earned him the nickname The Obscure. He taught that everything is in constant change and that the conflict between opposites keeps the world in balance. His short, provocative fragments inspired everyone from the Stoics to Hegel and Nietzsche.
ideas: Everything flows: reality is in permanent transformation
Opposites are united, and the tension between them creates the order of the world
There is a universal reason, the logos, that governs all things
heraclito.line: The Presocratics are the first Greek philosophers, before Socrates, who tried to explain nature without relying only on myths. Heraclitus is one of the most original of the group.

democrito.q: Nothing exists except atoms and empty space.
reading: The Presocratic Philosophers (Kirk, Raven and Schofield)
The Atomists: Leucippus and Democritus (C. C. W. Taylor)
democrito.bio: Democritus, together with his teacher Leucippus, proposed that everything is made of tiny, indivisible particles, the atoms, moving in the void. He wrote on physics, ethics and many other subjects, and was remembered as the laughing philosopher. His materialist view intuitively anticipated central ideas of modern science.
ideas: Everything that exists is made of indivisible atoms moving in the void
Qualities like color and taste depend on us, not on things in themselves
The good life is made of serenity and moderate joy, not excess
democrito.line: An atomist explains the world through the combination of atoms and void, with no divine intervention. Democritus is the greatest name of this school, alongside his teacher Leucippus.

protagoras.q: Man is the measure of all things.
protagoras.bio: Protagoras was the most celebrated of the sophists, teachers who charged fees to teach rhetoric and the art of winning debates. A friend of Pericles, he became known for the idea that the human being is the measure of all things. Plato criticized him harshly, but he was a pioneer in thinking about truth and values from human experience.
ideas: The human being is the measure of all things: truth depends on who perceives it
About the gods it is impossible to know whether they exist or not
On any subject there are arguments on both sides, and both can be defended
protagoras.line: Sophists were traveling teachers who taught oratory and politics, often doubting absolute truths. Protagoras is the most famous and the most respected of them.

socrates.q: I know that I know nothing.
socrates.bio: Socrates never wrote anything: he spent his days in the streets of Athens asking questions that showed people they did not know what they thought they knew. Accused of corrupting the young and disrespecting the gods, he was condemned to drink hemlock. We know his ideas through Plato and Xenophon, and he became the symbol of the philosopher.
ideas: Recognizing your own ignorance is the beginning of wisdom
An unexamined life is not worth living
No one does wrong on purpose: whoever acts badly acts out of ignorance
socrates.line: Socratic describes someone who follows Socrates' method of inquiring through dialogue and questions, seeking definitions and care of the soul. He is the origin of this approach.

platao.q: Cities will have no rest from evil until philosophers rule.
platao.bio: A student of Socrates, Plato founded the Academy in Athens, one of the first institutions of higher learning in the West. He wrote dialogues on justice, love, knowledge and politics that are still read around the world. His theory of Forms shaped philosophy and theology for more than two thousand years.
ideas: Beyond the sensible world lies the world of Forms, eternal and perfect
To know is to recall truths the soul contemplated before birth
The just city must be ruled by philosophers, who know the Good
platao.line: Idealist, here, means someone who considers ideas or forms more real than the material things we see. Plato is the founder of this view with his theory of Forms.

aristoteles.q: Man is by nature a political animal.
aristoteles.bio: A student of Plato for twenty years and later the tutor of Alexander the Great, Aristotle founded his own school, the Lyceum. He wrote on logic, biology, physics, ethics, politics and poetry, organizing nearly all the knowledge of his time. His work dominated Western and Islamic science and philosophy until the early modern era.
ideas: Happiness is the end of human life and is reached by practicing the virtues
Virtue is the mean between extremes, like courage between fear and recklessness
Human beings are political animals, who only flourish living in community
aristoteles.line: An Aristotelian follows Aristotle, valuing observation of the world, logic and the ethics of virtue. He is the founder of this tradition, later taken up by Arab thinkers and the Scholastics.

diogenes.q: I am a citizen of the world.
diogenes.b: Lives of the Eminent Philosophers (Diogenes Laertius)
diogenes.bio: Diogenes of Sinope lived in Athens as a beggar, sleeping in a large clay jar and scorning wealth and convention. The story goes that he asked Alexander the Great only to step out of his sun. With provocative acts, he showed that happiness depends on very little and that many social rules are artificial.
ideas: Happiness lies in living with the minimum, in accordance with nature
Social conventions, wealth and fame are illusions that enslave
The sage is a citizen of the world and owes loyalty to no single city
diogenes.line: Cynic comes from the Greek word for dog: the Cynics lived simply and without shame before convention. Diogenes is the most famous and radical representative of this school.

aristipo.q: I possess, but I am not possessed.
aristipo.b: Lives of the Eminent Philosophers (Diogenes Laertius)
reading: The Epistemology of the Cyrenaic School (Voula Tsouna)
aristipo.bio: Aristippus was a student of Socrates, but drew conclusions very different from Plato's. A native of Cyrene in North Africa, he held that the pleasure of the present moment is the greatest good. He lived comfortably at the courts of tyrants, always trying to enjoy life without being ruled by it.
ideas: Pleasure is the highest good, and pain is the evil to be avoided
Present, bodily pleasure is worth more than promises about the future
We should enjoy pleasures without becoming their slaves
aristipo.line: Cyrenaic comes from Cyrene, Aristippus' hometown, and names the school that saw immediate pleasure as the goal of life. Aristippus is considered its founder.

pirro.q: Nothing is more this than that.
reading: Pyrrho, His Antecedents, and His Legacy (Richard Bett)
pirro.bio: Pyrrho accompanied Alexander the Great on his expedition to India, where he is said to have met local sages. Back in Greece, he taught that we cannot know how things really are and that, for this reason, we should suspend judgment. He left no writings, but he gave his name to Pyrrhonian skepticism, which influenced Montaigne and Hume.
ideas: We cannot know with certainty how things are in themselves
Faced with opposing opinions, the best course is to suspend judgment
By suspending judgment, we reach tranquility of the soul
pirro.line: A skeptic doubts that secure knowledge is possible and prefers not to assert anything as definitive. Pyrrho is considered the father of this radical skepticism.

epicuro.bio: Epicurus founded the Garden in Athens, a community open even to women and slaves. He taught that the goal of life is pleasure, understood as the absence of pain in the body and disturbance in the soul. Far from the image of parties and excess, he advocated a simple life with friends, free from fear of the gods or of death.
ideas: Happiness is the absence of pain in the body and disturbance in the soul
Death is nothing to us, since when it arrives we no longer exist
Simple pleasures and friendship are worth more than luxury and power
epicuro.line: An Epicurean follows Epicurus in pursuing a calm, moderate pleasure, based on an atomist view of the world. He is the founder and great reference of the school.

seneca.q: It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste much of it.
seneca.bio: Born in Córdoba, in Hispania, Seneca was a writer, senator and adviser to Emperor Nero, who eventually ordered his death. In letters and essays, he spoke in practical terms about anger, grief, time and death. He is one of the most widely read Stoic authors today, precisely because he deals with everyday problems.
ideas: Life is not short: we are the ones who waste much of our time
We should prepare for adversity by imagining it before it happens
Wealth is not an evil, as long as the sage does not depend on it
seneca.line: A Stoic seeks to live according to reason and nature, accepting what is not up to us. Seneca represents Roman Stoicism turned toward practical life.

epicteto.q: It is not things that disturb us, but our opinions about them.
epicteto.bio: Epictetus was born a slave in Phrygia and taken to Rome, where he studied philosophy and later won his freedom. Expelled from Rome, he founded a school in Nicopolis. He wrote nothing, but his student Arrian recorded his teachings, which focus on the difference between what is and is not up to us.
ideas: Some things are up to us and others are not, and wisdom is knowing how to tell them apart
It is not events that disturb us, but the judgments we make about them
True freedom is inner, and no master can take it away
epicteto.line: A Stoic seeks serenity by living according to reason and accepting fate. Epictetus is the most direct and practical Stoic, focused on controlling our own judgments.

marco-aurelio.q: You have power over your mind, not over events.
reading: The Obstacle Is the Way (Ryan Holiday)
How to Think Like a Roman Emperor (Donald Robertson)
marco-aurelio.place: Rome and the frontiers of the Roman Empire
marco-aurelio.bio: Marcus Aurelius was emperor of Rome and spent much of his reign on military campaigns at the frontiers. In his spare hours, he wrote reflections to himself in Greek, which became known as the Meditations. The text shows a powerful man trying to be just, humble and serene, and it became a classic of practical wisdom.
ideas: We should accept with serenity what happens, for it is part of the order of the universe
All human beings are part of one rational community
Life is short, and each day should be lived with virtue and a sense of duty
marco-aurelio.line: A Stoic seeks virtue and inner peace by accepting what he cannot control. Marcus Aurelius shows Stoicism practiced by the man with the greatest power in the world.

plotino.q: Never stop sculpting your own statue.
reading: Plotinus or the Simplicity of Vision (Pierre Hadot)
plotino.bio: Plotinus studied in Alexandria and later taught philosophy in Rome, where he gathered a circle of students. His disciple Porphyry organized his writings into the Enneads. Plotinus reinterpreted Plato in a mystical vision in which everything proceeds from a supreme principle, the One, and he deeply influenced Christian, Jewish and Islamic thought.
ideas: Everything that exists emanates from a supreme and perfect principle, the One
Reality is hierarchical: from the One comes Intellect, and from it, Soul
The soul can return to the One through contemplation and purification
plotino.line: A Neoplatonist renews Plato with a spiritual vision in which everything is born from a single source and returns to it. Plotinus is the founder of this current.

santo-agostinho.q: Our heart is restless until it rests in You.
reading: On Free Choice of the Will
santo-agostinho.bio: Augustine was born in Thagaste, in present-day Algeria, and had a turbulent youth before converting to Christianity. He became bishop of Hippo and wrote decisive works such as the Confessions and The City of God. By joining Christian faith to Platonic philosophy, he became the most influential thinker of the early Middle Ages.
ideas: Evil is not a substance, but the absence or privation of good
Truth is within us and is illuminated by God
Divine grace is necessary for human beings to be able to do good
santo-agostinho.line: A Christian Neoplatonist uses the ideas of Plotinus and Plato to explain the Christian faith. Augustine is the great example, seeing God as the source of being and truth.

reading: Averroes: His Life, Works and Influence (Majid Fakhry)
averrois.bio: Ibn Rushd, known in the West as Averroes, was a judge, physician and philosopher in Muslim Córdoba. He wrote commentaries on Aristotle so thorough that Europeans simply called him The Commentator. He argued that philosophy and religion do not contradict each other, and his ideas stirred up the medieval Christian universities.
ideas: Philosophy and religion seek the same truth and cannot contradict each other
Those who are capable have a duty to study philosophy and use reason
Aristotle's work is the highest point of human knowledge
averrois.line: Falsafa is the Arabic name for Greek-inspired philosophy in the Islamic world, and Aristotelian means one who follows Aristotle. Averroes is the greatest Aristotelian of this tradition.

maimonides.q: Of God, we know only what He is not.
maimonides.bio: Moses Maimonides was born in Córdoba, but fled with his family from religious persecution and settled in Cairo, where he was court physician and leader of the Jewish community. He organized Jewish law and wrote the Guide for the Perplexed for those who felt torn between faith and reason. He is the greatest Jewish philosopher of the Middle Ages.
ideas: Faith and reason can be harmonized, and the Bible can also be read allegorically
Of God we can only say what He is not, since He surpasses our concepts
Studying and observing the law perfects both the individual and society
maimonides.line: Jewish philosophy is the reflection that joins biblical and rabbinic tradition with Greek philosophy. Maimonides is its central figure, reconciling the Torah with Aristotle.

tomas-de-aquino.q: Grace does not destroy nature, but perfects it.
tomas-de-aquino.bio: Thomas Aquinas was an Italian Dominican friar who taught at the University of Paris. In the Summa Theologica, he united Aristotle's philosophy with Christian faith in a broad, organized system. Canonized and declared a Doctor of the Church, he remains the main philosophical reference of Catholicism today.
ideas: Reason and faith do not oppose each other, since both come from God
It is possible to demonstrate the existence of God through five rational ways
There is a natural law, accessible to reason, that guides moral good
tomas-de-aquino.line: A Scholastic is a thinker of the medieval universities who used logic and debate to reconcile faith and reason. Thomas Aquinas is the high point of Scholasticism.

guilherme-de-ockham.q: Entities must not be multiplied beyond necessity.
reading: Ockham's Theory of Terms: Part I of the Summa Logicae
A Short Discourse on Tyrannical Government
guilherme-de-ockham.bio: William of Ockham was an English Franciscan friar who studied at Oxford. He got into conflicts with the pope over the poverty of the Church and ended up taking refuge in Munich, under the emperor's protection. He is remembered for Ockham's razor, the principle that says not to multiply explanations without need.
ideas: We should not assume more entities than necessary to explain something
Only individual things exist, and universals are merely names and concepts
The pope's power has limits and must not override civil power
guilherme-de-ockham.line: A nominalist holds that general concepts, like humanity, are only names, and that only individuals exist. Ockham is the greatest defender of this thesis in the Middle Ages.

joao-calvino.q: The human heart is a perpetual factory of idols.
reading: The Golden Booklet of the True Christian Life
joao-calvino.bio: Jean Calvin was born in France, studied law and joined the Protestant Reformation, having to flee the country. In Geneva, he organized a church and a city according to strict biblical principles. His Institutes became the foundation of Reformed Protestantism, which spread through Switzerland, the Netherlands, Scotland and North America.
ideas: God is sovereign over everything, and only his grace saves human beings
God chose from eternity who will be saved, known as predestination
The Bible is the highest authority in matters of faith, above tradition
joao-calvino.line: Reformer refers to the leaders of the 16th-century Protestant Reformation, who broke with Rome. Calvin is one of the main ones, founder of the Reformed or Calvinist tradition.

maquiavel.q: It is better to be feared than loved, if you cannot be both.
maquiavel.bio: Niccolò Machiavelli was a diplomat and official of the Florentine republic. Removed from power when the Medici returned, he wrote The Prince, a manual on how to win and keep power. For describing politics as it is, and not as it should be, he was called cynical, but also the founder of modern political science.
ideas: Politics has its own rules, separate from religious and private morality
The ideal ruler is both feared and loved, but if he cannot be both, it is better to be feared
Fortune governs half of events, and the leader's virtue decides the rest
maquiavel.line: A political realist analyzes power as it actually works, without moral idealization. Machiavelli is the great founder of this way of thinking about politics.

reading: Journal of Montaigne's Travels in Italy
How to Live: Or a Life of Montaigne (Sarah Bakewell)
montaigne.bio: Michel de Montaigne was a French nobleman who, after years in public life, withdrew to his tower to read and write. He created a new genre, the essay, in which he examined himself and human customs with frankness and humor. He lived through the wars of religion and defended tolerance and doubt in the face of certainties.
ideas: Our knowledge is limited and uncertain, and we should doubt our certainties
Customs vary among peoples, and what we call barbarian is just the different
Knowing yourself is the path to living well and with moderation
montaigne.line: A humanist skeptic joins the doubt of the ancient skeptics with the Renaissance interest in the human being. Montaigne applies the suspension of judgment to the observation of himself and of customs.

descartes.bio: René Descartes was a French philosopher, mathematician and scientist, creator of analytic geometry. He lived much of his life in the Netherlands and died in Stockholm, at the invitation of Queen Christina. He decided to doubt everything in order to find a secure foundation for knowledge, and is therefore considered the father of modern philosophy.
ideas: We should doubt everything that can be doubted to find something certain
I think, therefore I am: the existence of thought is the first certainty
Mind and body are distinct substances, one thinking and the other extended
descartes.line: A rationalist believes that reason, not the senses, is the main source of secure knowledge. Descartes inaugurates modern rationalism with his method.

pascal.q: The heart has its reasons, which reason knows nothing of.
pascal.bio: Blaise Pascal was a precocious genius: he invented a mechanical calculator and contributed to probability theory and physics. After an intense religious experience, he devoted himself to defending Christianity. His Pensées, published after his death, show human greatness and wretchedness and the limits of reason.
ideas: The heart knows truths that reason alone cannot reach
Betting on the existence of God is the wisest choice in the face of uncertainty
The human being is as frail as a reed, but a reed that thinks
pascal.line: A fideist holds that faith, not reason, is the main path to religious truths. Pascal maintains that reason has limits and only faith reaches God.

spinoza.q: Not to laugh, not to lament, but to understand.
reading: Treatise on the Emendation of the Intellect
spinoza.bio: Baruch Spinoza was born into a Portuguese Jewish family in Amsterdam and was expelled from the community for his ideas. He lived modestly, grinding lenses, while writing the Ethics, organized like a geometry book. He defended freedom of thought and a view in which God and nature are the same thing.
ideas: God and nature are a single infinite substance
Everything happens by necessity, and freedom lies in understanding the causes
Freedom of thought and expression is essential to a healthy state
spinoza.line: A rationalist trusts reason to reach fundamental truths. Spinoza takes this to the extreme, deducing all of reality as if it were geometry.

leibniz.q: This is the best of all possible worlds.
leibniz.bio: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz was a philosopher, mathematician, diplomat and librarian in the service of the court of Hanover. He invented infinitesimal calculus at the same time as Newton and imagined calculating machines. For him, the universe is made of simple units, the monads, and God chose to create the best of all possible worlds.
ideas: The real world is the best of all possible worlds
Reality is made of monads, simple and spiritual units
Nothing happens without a sufficient reason that explains why it is so
leibniz.line: An optimistic rationalist trusts reason to explain everything and believes the world is good. Leibniz is the example, with his thesis of the best of all possible worlds.

thomas-hobbes.q: The life of man is solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short.
thomas-hobbes.bio: Thomas Hobbes lived through the English Civil War and spent years in exile in Paris. In Leviathan, he argued that without a strong government, human life would be a war of all against all. His theory of the social contract, based on fear and the search for security, founded modern political philosophy.
ideas: Without a state, human life would be solitary, poor, brutal and short
People make a contract and hand power to a sovereign in exchange for security
The sovereign needs strong, indivisible power to prevent civil war
thomas-hobbes.line: A contractarian explains the state as the result of an agreement among people. Hobbes is the first great modern contractarian and defends a strong sovereign.

john-locke.q: Where there is no law, there is no freedom.
john-locke.bio: John Locke was an English physician and philosopher, involved in the political disputes that led to the Glorious Revolution of 1688. He argued that everyone has natural rights to life, liberty and property, and that government exists to protect them. His ideas inspired American independence and liberal democracies.
ideas: Everyone is born with natural rights to life, liberty and property
Government depends on the consent of the people, who may rebel against tyranny
The mind is born as a blank slate and learns through experience
john-locke.line: A classical liberal defends individual rights, limited government and religious toleration. Locke is considered the father of political liberalism.

george-berkeley.q: To be is to be perceived.
george-berkeley.b: A Treatise Concerning the Principles of Human Knowledge
reading: Three Dialogues between Hylas and Philonous
An Essay Towards a New Theory of Vision
george-berkeley.bio: George Berkeley was an Irish philosopher and Anglican bishop of Cloyne. While still young, he proposed a surprising thesis: material objects do not exist outside the mind, because to be is to be perceived. He also tried to found a college in Bermuda and spent a few years in North America.
ideas: To be is to be perceived: things exist only while they are perceived
There is no matter that exists independently of any mind
God perceives everything continuously and guarantees the stability of the world
george-berkeley.line: An empiricist idealist starts from the experience of the senses, like the empiricists, but concludes that only minds and ideas exist. Berkeley is the main name of this position.

david-hume.q: Reason is, and ought only to be, the slave of the passions.
david-hume.bio: A Scottish philosopher and historian, Hume was one of the sharpest minds of the Enlightenment. He took empiricism to its ultimate consequences and showed that many everyday certainties, like the idea of cause and effect, come from habit and not from pure reason. His skepticism woke Kant and still shapes debates about science, morality and religion.
ideas: All ideas are copies of impressions that arrived through the senses
We do not see causation: we expect the future to repeat the past out of sheer habit
Reason alone moves no one; it is passions and feelings that decide
david-hume.line: Empiricism says that all knowledge comes from experience, not from innate ideas. Hume is the most radical empiricist: he used this principle to show the limits of what reason can prove.

voltaire.bio: Voltaire, pen name of François-Marie Arouet, was a tireless writer, playwright and polemicist. He used irony as a weapon against religious fanaticism, censorship and the abuses of the Church and monarchy, even being jailed and exiled. His tales, like Candide, and his campaigns for victims of injustice made him the face of the French Enlightenment.
ideas: Religious tolerance is a condition for a civilized and peaceful society
Fanaticism and superstition are the greatest enemies of human reason
Naive optimism does not solve the world's evil; it is better to work and act
voltaire.line: The Enlightenment was the 18th-century movement that trusted reason, science and free debate to fight blind tradition. Voltaire was its most famous and combative popularizer.

rousseau.q: Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains.
rousseau.bio: Born in Geneva, Rousseau was a philosopher, writer and even composer, a restless and controversial figure. He argued that human beings are born good and are corrupted by society, property and inequality. His ideas on popular sovereignty inspired the French Revolution, and his valuing of feeling paved the way for Romanticism.
ideas: Human beings are good by nature; it is unequal society that corrupts them
A legitimate government arises from a pact and expresses the general will of the people
Education should respect the child's nature, not stifle it
rousseau.line: Contractarians explain the state as the result of an agreement among people; Romantics value feeling and nature. Rousseau joins both: a social pact in service of natural goodness.

adam-smith.q: It is not from the benevolence of the butcher that we expect our dinner.
adam-smith.bio: A professor of moral philosophy in Glasgow, Adam Smith is remembered as the father of modern economics. In The Wealth of Nations, he explained how the division of labor and free exchange generate prosperity. Before that, he wrote about sympathy as the basis of morality, showing that his economic thought had ethical roots.
ideas: When each person pursues their own interest, the market tends to generate wealth for all
The division of labor multiplies a society's productivity
Morality arises from sympathy: we put ourselves in another's place to judge
adam-smith.line: Economic liberalism defends free markets, property and little state interference in the economy. Adam Smith is its classical founder, with the idea that free exchange organizes society.

edmund-burke.q: Society is a partnership between the dead, the living, and those yet to be born.
edmund-burke.b: Reflections on the Revolution in France
reading: A Philosophical Enquiry into the Origin of Our Ideas of the Sublime and Beautiful
edmund-burke.bio: Born in Dublin, Burke was a politician and writer in the British Parliament for decades. He supported the cause of the American colonists, but attacked the French Revolution fiercely, predicting it would end in terror and tyranny. For this he is seen as the father of modern conservatism, which distrusts abrupt change guided only by theories.
ideas: Old institutions hold wisdom accumulated over many generations
Reforms should be gradual; revolutions in the name of abstract theories destroy
Society unites those who have died, those who live, and those yet to be born
edmund-burke.line: Conservatism values tradition, prudence and continuity, preferring to reform rather than break. Burke is its main reference, defending historical inheritance against revolution.

joseph-de-maistre.q: Every nation gets the government it deserves.
reading: The Crooked Timber of Humanity (Isaiah Berlin)
joseph-de-maistre.place: Chambéry, Savoy, and Saint Petersburg, Russia
joseph-de-maistre.bio: A diplomat and writer from Savoy, Maistre spent years in Saint Petersburg as ambassador of the king of Sardinia. He was the fiercest critic of the French Revolution and the Enlightenment, which he saw as a revolt against God. He defended the pope and the king as the foundations of social order and influenced European counterrevolutionary thought.
ideas: The French Revolution was a divine punishment for the sins of the age
Strong authority, of king and pope, is needed to maintain order
Written constitutions count for little; the true foundation of a people is tradition
joseph-de-maistre.line: A reactionary not only preserves but wants to return to an order before a rupture. Maistre wanted to restore the world before the Revolution, with throne and altar at the center.

kant.b: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals
kant.bio: Immanuel Kant spent practically his whole life in Königsberg, famous for his methodical routine. Even so, he revolutionized philosophy by proposing that the mind organizes experience, uniting rationalism and empiricism. He also created an ethics based on duty and the dignity of each person, which still underlies the idea of human rights.
ideas: We know things only as they appear to us, never as they are in themselves
Act only according to rules you would accept as valid for everyone
Persons are ends in themselves and can never be treated merely as means
kant.line: Transcendental idealism is the thesis that the world we know is shaped by the structures of the mind itself, such as space and time. Kant created this view to explain how secure knowledge is possible.

mary-wollstonecraft.q: I do not wish women to have power over men, but over themselves.
mary-wollstonecraft.b: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
reading: A Vindication of the Rights of Men
Letters Written in Sweden, Norway, and Denmark
mary-wollstonecraft.bio: An English writer of modest origins, Mary Wollstonecraft supported herself as a teacher, translator and author. In 1792 she published A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, arguing that women only seemed inferior for lack of education. She died young, days after giving birth to her daughter, the future author of Frankenstein, Mary Shelley.
ideas: Supposed female inferiority comes from lack of education, not from nature
Women and men have the same reason and deserve the same rights
Marriage should be a friendship between equals, not a form of submission
mary-wollstonecraft.line: Liberal feminism seeks equal rights, education and opportunities for women through reason and law. Wollstonecraft is its pioneer, applying Enlightenment ideals to women.

jeremy-bentham.q: The greatest happiness of the greatest number.
jeremy-bentham.b: An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation
jeremy-bentham.bio: A jurist and English reformer, Bentham wanted to transform laws and institutions based on a calculation of pleasure and pain. He defended ideas far ahead of his time, such as wider voting rights, an end to cruel punishments and consideration for animals. He asked that his body be preserved, and it is still on display at University College London.
ideas: The right is what produces the greatest happiness for the greatest number of people
Pleasure and pain are the only real guides to human behavior
The suffering of animals counts too, since they can feel pain
jeremy-bentham.line: Utilitarianism judges actions and laws by their consequences: the best is what produces the most well-being overall, adding up the happiness of everyone affected. Bentham was the systematic founder of this current.

hegel.q: What is rational is real, and what is real is rational.
hegel.b: Lectures on the Philosophy of History
reading: Elements of the Philosophy of Right
hegel.bio: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel was a professor in Jena, Heidelberg and Berlin, where he became the most influential philosopher in Germany. He built an enormous system in which history, art, religion and the state are stages in the development of Spirit. His dialectic inspired admirers and critics alike, from Marx to the existentialists.
ideas: Reality develops through conflicts and overcomings, in a dialectical movement
History is the path by which human freedom is realized
We recognize ourselves as subjects through the recognition of others
hegel.line: German idealism was the post-Kant current that saw reason or spirit as the basis of all reality. Hegel is its culmination, with a system that embraces nature, history and culture.

schopenhauer.q: Man can do what he wills, but he cannot will what he wills.
schopenhauer.b: Aphorisms on the Wisdom of Life
reading: The World as Will and Representation
schopenhauer.bio: Arthur Schopenhauer was a German philosopher of difficult temperament, an avowed rival of Hegel. He taught that behind the world lies a blind and insatiable Will, the source of constant desire and suffering. One of the first Westerners to study Buddhism and Hinduism, he influenced Nietzsche, Freud, Wagner and many writers.
ideas: Behind everything lies a blind Will that is never satisfied
Life swings between the pain of unfulfilled desire and boredom
Compassion for the suffering of others is the true basis of morality
schopenhauer.line: Philosophical pessimism is the view that existence brings more pain than joy and that the world has no good purpose. Schopenhauer is its great representative, proposing renunciation of desire as the way out.

auguste-comte.q: Love as a principle, order as the basis, progress as the goal.
reading: The Positive Philosophy of Auguste Comte (Harriet Martineau)
auguste-comte.bio: Auguste Comte was a French thinker who founded positivism and gave sociology its name. He believed humanity passes through stages and would arrive at an era guided by science. His ideas left a deep mark on Brazil: the motto Order and Progress on the flag comes directly from him, and a Positivist Church still exists there today.
ideas: Humanity evolves from a religious stage to the metaphysical and, finally, the scientific
Only knowledge based on observation and verifiable laws is reliable
Society can be studied scientifically, as physics studies nature
auguste-comte.line: Positivism holds that only science, grounded in observable facts, produces valid knowledge, and that it should guide society. Comte is the creator and main name of this doctrine.

john-stuart-mill.q: Over himself, the individual is sovereign.
john-stuart-mill.bio: Educated with extreme intensity by his father, John Stuart Mill was learning Greek at the age of three. He became the most influential liberal philosopher of the 19th century, defending individual liberty, democracy and equality between the sexes. He served as a member of Parliament and wrote, with Harriet Taylor, pioneering texts on women's rights.
ideas: The state may limit someone only to prevent harm to others
Freedom of thought and discussion helps truth to emerge
There are higher pleasures, like those of the intellect, that are worth more than others
john-stuart-mill.line: Liberal utilitarianism combines the pursuit of the greatest well-being with a firm defense of individual liberties. Mill refined Bentham's utilitarianism and tied it to political liberalism.

henry-david-thoreau.q: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately.
henry-david-thoreau.bio: An American writer and naturalist, Thoreau spent two years in a cabin by Walden Pond to live simply. He refused to pay a tax he saw as supporting slavery and the war against Mexico, and spent a night in jail. His essay on civil disobedience inspired Gandhi, Martin Luther King and environmentalists.
ideas: Living simply frees us from consumption and reveals what really matters
Nature is a source of wisdom, health and spiritual renewal
It is legitimate to peacefully disobey a government that commits injustice
henry-david-thoreau.line: Transcendentalism was an American movement that valued intuition, nature and individual autonomy over institutions. Thoreau put it into practice, living by Walden Pond.

kierkegaard.q: Life can only be understood backwards, but it must be lived forwards.
kierkegaard.bio: Søren Kierkegaard was a Danish thinker who wrote under several pseudonyms and criticized his country's official Church. For him, faith is not a set of doctrines but a personal and anguished choice before God. He is considered the father of existentialism for placing the concrete individual at the center of philosophy.
ideas: The truth that matters is subjective, the one by which one lives and dies
Anxiety arises from awareness of freedom and of possibilities
Faith is a personal leap that goes beyond reason and demands risk
kierkegaard.line: Christian existentialism focuses on individual existence, choice and anxiety, understood within a personal relationship with God. Kierkegaard is its founder and main reference.

reading: The False Principle of Our Education
max-stirner.bio: Max Stirner, pen name of Johann Kaspar Schmidt, was a teacher in Berlin and frequented the circle of the Young Hegelians. In The Ego and Its Own, he attacked God, the state, morality and even humanity as ideas that enslave the individual. He died poor and almost forgotten, but was rediscovered by anarchists and existentialists.
ideas: God, state, morality and humanity are ghosts that dominate the individual
Each person should take themselves as their own cause, serving no outside ideals
Instead of the state, he proposes a free union of egoists who join out of interest
max-stirner.line: Stirner's egoism is the thesis that the unique individual is the only real value, free from duties imposed by abstract ideas. He is the creator of this radical position, close to individualist anarchism.

reading: System of Economical Contradictions: Or, The Philosophy of Misery
proudhon.bio: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon was a self-taught printer and the first thinker to call himself an anarchist. He became famous for declaring that property is theft, criticizing those who live on rent without working. He served as a deputy, ended up jailed for his writings, and influenced the French labor movement and syndicalism.
ideas: Property that yields income without work is a form of exploitation
Society can organize itself without government, through free agreements
Power should be decentralized into federations of autonomous communities
proudhon.line: Mutualist anarchism proposes a stateless society based on fair exchange, cooperation and mutual credit among workers. Proudhon is its founder and the first self-declared anarchist.

mikhail-bakunin.q: The passion for destruction is also a creative passion.
mikhail-bakunin.place: Russia, Switzerland and other European countries
mikhail-bakunin.bio: A Russian revolutionary of noble family, Bakunin took part in uprisings across Europe, spent years in prison and was exiled to Siberia, from where he escaped. In the First International, he broke with Marx over the idea of using the state to reach socialism. He became the main reference of collectivist anarchism.
ideas: The state, even if run by workers, always creates a new oppressive elite
Liberty without equality is privilege; equality without liberty is slavery
Revolution must come from the organized masses, from the bottom up
mikhail-bakunin.line: Anarchism defends the abolition of the state and of all imposed authority, replacing them with free associations among equals. Bakunin is its great revolutionary and collectivist name.

karl-marx.q: The philosophers have only interpreted the world; the point is to change it.
karl-marx.bio: Born in Trier, Germany, Karl Marx spent much of his life in exile in London, often in poverty. With Friedrich Engels, he wrote the Communist Manifesto and devoted decades to Capital, a critical analysis of capitalism. His ideas shaped labor movements, revolutions and the social sciences worldwide.
ideas: History is driven by the struggle between social classes
Material and economic conditions shape ideas, laws and culture
Capitalist profit comes from the unpaid labor of workers
karl-marx.line: Historical materialism explains society from how humans produce their material life and the class relations that arise from it. Marx created it as the basis of his critique of capitalism.

nietzsche.bio: Friedrich Nietzsche became a professor in Basel at 24, but fragile health made him live as a wanderer across Europe. He announced the death of God and questioned the moral values inherited from Christianity. Writing in brilliant aphorisms, he influenced the philosophy, literature and psychology of the 20th century.
ideas: With the death of God, traditional values lose their foundation
There are no pure facts, only interpretations made from perspectives
Each person must create their own values and overcome themselves
nietzsche.line: Perspectivism is the idea that all knowledge is an interpretation made from some point of view, with no neutral view from nowhere. Nietzsche is its main author.

william-james.q: Faith in a fact can help create the fact.
william-james.bio: Trained as a physician, William James was a professor at Harvard and one of the founders of modern psychology. He helped create pragmatism, which evaluates ideas by the practical effects they produce in life. He also wrote on religious experience and the will to believe, always in a clear and accessible style.
ideas: An idea is true to the extent that it works and makes a practical difference
Consciousness is a continuous stream, not a sum of isolated pieces
Facing vital choices without definitive proof, we have the right to believe
william-james.line: Pragmatism is an American current that measures ideas by their practical consequences, not by an abstract correspondence with reality. William James was its greatest popularizer.
